title: The 1933 European trip, Rose's wedding and Mills's no-wives rule
summary: Rose recalls they married just before the first European trip, Rose didn't go, and Mills refused wives on tour.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah. Tell me about the trips to
Europe. The first one was in 1933, wasn't it?
Yeah. That's when we got married, at St. Mark's Catholic Church; we had gotten married just before they left.
That's a picture of Rose and me on the boat, before we left.
Oh, what a beautiful picture. That is really nice.
I was kind of fat then.
Oh, Rose was a very good looking woman.
Pretty Big in the behind; she was big, you know? Well, anyhow, we took that picture over there, and when we left she went home, because she didn't go with me that time.
Irving Mills said that everybody in the band wanted to take their wives, and he absolutely would not stand for it.
